title: Project P.I.T.T.
genre: Physics sandbox / automation-factory / idle-incremental (feed rubber ducks to a giant pit)
release_date: 2026-08-19 (Steam, PC) [CONFIRMED – Pirate PR press release / Steam store / TechTimes 2026-08-21]
early_access_date: no data (no Early Access found; itch.io demo/prototype preceded Steam release; Steam demo app 4636730)
team_size: 1 (solo dev) [per task brief, Pirate PR press release and DLCompare describe a solo developer; not independently re-verified with a dev quote in this session]
country: France [per task brief; not re-verified in this session]
developer_background: Solo dev who first released a free itch.io version (65k+ downloads per task brief) that went viral through YouTube let's-players, then signed with publisher Pretty Soon for the Steam release. No data on earlier commercial titles.
publisher: Pretty Soon [per task brief / Steam store]; publisher–dev revenue split undisclosed
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4026250/Project_PITT/ ; Steam demo: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4636730/Project_PITT_Demo/ ; itch.io demo: https://fr0ke.itch.io/project-pitt-demo
business_model: Premium $9.99 [CONFIRMED – Steam store]; 15% launch discount through 2026-09-02 [TechTimes]; later 20% off ($7.99) and a bundle with 'Sort Them Ducks' at $12.04 [Steam store snapshot]. Free demo on Steam and itch.io.
units_or_downloads: 22,000+ copies in first 24 hours (2026-08-19/20) and 50,000+ copies about 5 days later (~2026-08-24) [CONFIRMED – developer figures reported by DLCompare]. Current (2026-10-08): ~60,000–75,000 Steam units [ESTIMATE – ~1,000–1,050 reviews × 60 (cheap, YouTube-viral, implied ratio ≥50 from dev data) ]. Raijin shows only ~22,300 units (medium confidence) – clearly an under-estimate vs dev data. itch.io free version: 65,000+ downloads [per task brief; not re-verified].
peak_concurrent_players: no data (Steam CCU tracker pages for app 4026250 were not retrieved before the search budget ran out)
steam_reviews: 1,000+ reviews, ~79% positive ('Mostly Positive') on ~2026-10-08 [Steam store snapshot]; 920 reviews, 80% positive on an earlier tracker snapshot [Raijin].
implied_review_multiplier: n/a for same date; lower bound ≈ 50 (50,000 confirmed units by ~2026-08-24 ÷ ~1,000 reviews by Oct 2026; reviews were fewer on Aug 24, so the same-date ratio was higher than 50)
gross_revenue: $400,000+ gross by ~2026-08-24 (≈50k units) [CONFIRMED – dev figures via DLCompare]. Current: ~$450k–$560k [ESTIMATE – 60k–75k units × $7.49 (list $9.99 × 0.75)]. Raijin estimate ~$187k (medium confidence; inconsistent with dev data, disregarded).
net_revenue: ~$290k–$365k to developer + publisher combined [ESTIMATE – gross × (1 − 30% Steam cut) × 0.93 refunds]; Froke/Pretty Soon split unknown.
production_cost: no data on dev time, so no disclosed cost. Illustrative: solo France at ~$6k/month → ~$72k opportunity cost per year of full-time development [ESTIMATE – spec rate]; publisher Pretty Soon likely funded PR (Pirate PR campaign) and possibly porting/QA (no data).
development_time: no data (itch.io prototype/demo preceded the Aug 2026 Steam launch; start date not found)
why_popular: Absurd, instantly readable premise: an automation/idle physics sandbox where you mass-produce rubber ducks and feed them to a giant pit – the 'number go up' idle loop made visible as tens of thousands of physical ducks (Kotaku: 'I tanked my framerate by making 100,000 rubber ducks'). Satisfying chaos and escalating physics spectacle is perfect YouTube thumbnail/let's-play content; mystery framing ('This job is a ducking nightmare').
marketing_channels: Free itch.io version (65k+ downloads) → big YouTube creators GrayStillPlays, ImCade, DangerouslyFunny (10M+ combined views per press release) → Steam page and demo → ~115k–120k wishlists at launch (Froke) → publisher Pretty Soon + Pirate PR press release; launch discount; bundle with another duck game ('Sort Them Ducks'); press (Kotaku, TechTimes, AllKeyShop, DLCompare).
engine: no data (not found before search budget ran out)
art_style: no data in detail; rubber-duck factory/pit theme with mass physics objects (100k+ ducks on screen, per Kotaku).
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the idle/automation economy, upgrade trees, conveyor/factory logic, save system and UI; generate duck/prop models and textures, SFX (squeaks!) and music; draft store copy. | AI cannot: make 100k physics objects run smoothly (needs careful profiling – ECS/DOTS, GPU instancing, object pooling, sleeping bodies), balance idle pacing so it stays compelling for hours, design the 'mystery' framing, or win over YouTubers. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (DOTS/ECS physics) or Godot 4 (Jolt + MultiMesh), Meshy/Tripo for props, Scenario/Midjourney for UI, ElevenLabs SFX, Suno music, GodotSteam/Steamworks.NET.
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 3–6 weeks, ~$150–$500 (Claude Pro/Max, small 3D/audio subs, $100 Steam Direct optional for itch-first launch). Excludes developer living costs.
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–8 months, ~$2,000–$7,000 (subs, performance-optimisation asset packs, capsule art, playtests, creator outreach/PR). Excludes developer living costs; a publisher may cover PR in exchange for a revenue share.

data_conflicts: Units: dev-reported 50k+ within ~5 days (DLCompare) vs Raijin ~22.3k total (medium confidence) – used dev data, Raijin disregarded. Gross: dev $400k+ vs Raijin $187k – used dev. Wishlists: 115k at launch (task brief/press) vs ~120k (Froke via DLCompare). Reviews: 920 @ 80% (Raijin, earlier) vs 1,000+ @ 79% (Steam store, later) – consistent over time. Discount: 15% intro (TechTimes) vs 20% later promo (Steam snapshot) – different dates.
notes: INCOMPLETE: research cut short by the shared WebSearch budget (200/turn) after one search for this game. Missing: peak CCU (check steamdb.info/app/4026250/charts), engine, dev time, confirmation of France/solo. Lesson for a solo creator: ship a free itch.io prototype of a single absurd, visually escalating idea, get picked up by big YouTube let's-players, then convert that to Steam wishlists (with a publisher handling PR). The 'Mostly Positive' 79% suggests the paid version's depth/performance did not satisfy everyone – the hook outsold the content.
